messages:
jamie: infra-bot fired an alert for hosted-inference-prod (eu-west) — sustained 5xx + timeouts starting ~15:23 UTC. customers reporting failed requests and increased latency. opening warroom here.
infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-inference-prod eu-west - 5xx rate 18% over 5m, median latency 1.8s -> 3.6s, kv_cache_miss_rate spike. Incident ID: inc-5160004321
ada: oncall joining. any quick repros or request patterns? link to grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123
rob: seeing gateway 503s then 502s from model-proxy. logs show repeated `upstream reset by peer`. also spike in long-seq requests (>=4096 tokens). sample failing call from trace:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-large","input":"<long user prompt>"}'
```
rob: relevant log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T15:22:47Z gateway ERROR upsteam reset by peer id=proxy-7c
2026-03-15T15:22:47Z proxy  WARN kvcache miss 98% seq_len=4096
2026-03-15T15:22:48Z batcher ERROR queue_wait > 1200ms
```
sasha: support here — Customer SC-2345 and SC-2299 reported ~30% error rate this morning, some saw duplicate billing attempts due to retries. have both customer traces saved.
jamie: initial triage hypothesis: long-context requests pushed model runtime beyond expected tail latencies -> batcher backlog -> conn pool exhaustion -> gateway circuit tripped. also KV-cache warmup failures made it worse.
ada: immediate mitigations we can do now:
- route traffic for hosted-prod-eu-west -> fallback model `redwood-lite-v1` (smaller, lower memory) for new incoming requests
- increase gateway circuit-breaker thresholds temporarily
- throttle/heavy-rate-limit customers that are generating long-context traffic
I'll apply routing rule and bump cb thresholds now.
ops-oncall: applying routing rule to 30% -> will ramp to 100% over 5m. setting per-tenant rate limit for top offenders. disabling batcher coalescing for long sequences to reduce head-of-line blocking.
rob: confirmed after routing change 5xx dropped from 18% -> 2.3% in 7 minutes. kvcache miss rate improving. moving to monitoring window.
jamie: customer comms: @sasha can you draft a short note explaining incident + mitigation + ETA for root fix? include that we routed to a smaller model and are investigating backpressure.
sasha: draft posted to #support-desk: "We're seeing elevated errors; we've routed traffic to a lower-latency model and disabled aggressive batching for long requests. We'll follow up with a root cause and ETA for elastic fix." awaiting legal ok before send.
ada: proposing postmortem action items (short form):
1) batcher backpressure tuning + adaptive batching for long-context requests (owner: rob)
2) gateway conn-pool autoscale + better circuit-breaker hysteresis (owner: ada)
3) KV-cache prewarm + detection for cold starts on new deployments (owner: infra-team)
4) automatic fallback routing playbook + runbook update (owner: ada)
5) billing retry dedupe check for support edge cases (owner: pm-lee)
6) add synthetic long-context load tests to perf-suite (owner: rob)
pm-lee: adding a ticket for billing dedupe and customer refunds if applicable. target: investigative PR by 2026-03-22.
ops-oncall: created incident ticket INC-5160004321 in Jira, linking traces and Grafana panels. moving incident severity P1 -> P2 as metrics normalized.
infra-bot: RESOLVED: metrics back to baseline for 10m window. 5xx < 1%, median latency back to expected. Incident closed from active response. Follow-ups assigned in Jira.
jamie: thanks everyone — quick retrospective at 10:30 tomorrow to go over action owners and ETA. :thumbsup:
sasha: will send customer notification after legal review. closing the warroom thread. :heart:
